basic_details.scholarship_name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Cybersecurity (CYBERUS)
basic_details.offering_entity: European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA) & CYBERUS Consortium
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: Université de Bretagne Sud (UBS - Lorient/Vannes, France), Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB - Brussels, Belgium), University of Tartu (UT - Tartu, Estonia)
degree_levels: Master of Science (MSc / Joint or Double Degree)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Cybersecurity, IoT Security, Software Security, Cryptography, Network Defense, Embedded Systems Security, and Threat Intelligence.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~20 to 24 prestigious Erasmus Mundus scholarship grants awarded globally per cohort
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open globally under Partner Country quota; typically 2 to 4 Pakistani scholars selected per intake
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: 24 months (2 full academic years across at least two European countries)

nationality_requirements: Open to candidates from all countries worldwide, including Pakistan (Partner Country category)
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No age restriction under Erasmus Mundus programme regulations.
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Recognized 4-year Bachelor of Science (BS / BSc 16-year) in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or Computer Engineering with minimum CGPA 3.30 / 4.00 (75%+).
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum CGPA 3.30 / 4.00; competitive applicants typically hold CGPA >= 3.65 / 4.00.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Solid foundation in computer networks, operating systems, discrete mathematics, computer architecture, cryptography, and programming (C/C++, Python).
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated or enrolled in final undergraduate year graduating prior to July 31 preceding September intake.
eligibility_requirements.graduation_year_restrictions: No restriction on year of graduation.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Participation in Capture The Flag (CTF) security competitions, security certifications (CEH, OSCP), or security bug bounties strongly valued.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic minimum 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or TOEFL iBT minimum 90 (no section below 20). MOI certificates are not accepted by CYBERUS consortium.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Consortium languages (French, Dutch, Estonian) are not required; instruction is 100% in English.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Erasmus Mundus NDICI / IPA III Partner Country scholarship quota applies to Pakistani nationals.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Candidates who have previously benefited from an Erasmus Mundus Master or Doctoral scholarship are ineligible.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full tuition fee waiver across all partner universities (worth EUR 18,000 for non-EU students).

admission_application_fee.details: Direct application via CYBERUS consortium portal is completely free.

accommodation.details: Covered directly from the EUR 1,400 / month living allowance; partner universities assist with student residence reservations.

monthly_stipend.details: EUR 1,400 / month tax-free living allowance for up to 24 months (total EUR 33,600 | ~PKR 425,000 / month).

airfare.details: EUR 3,000 per year travel and mobility contribution for Partner Country students living >4,000 km away.

visa_fee.details: EUR 1,000 installation grant covers visa processing, medical attestations, and initial arrival logistics.

health_insurance.details: Full worldwide comprehensive health, emergency, and travel insurance meeting Erasmus+ requirements.

food_allowance.details: Covered via monthly EUR 1,400 living stipend plus access to subsidized campus cafeterias across France, Belgium, and Estonia.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Full access to specialized cyber range environments, virtual labs, and digital scientific libraries.
books_and_materials_allowance.amount: Full university library and cyber range access

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Master thesis internship placements in partner industrial cybersecurity labs (ANSSI, Thales, Airbus Cybersecurity, NATO CCDCOE).

travel_transit_allowance.details: Mobility travel grant between consortium host nations.
travel_transit_allowance.amount: Covered via Erasmus mobility travel budget

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Multiple host institutions (Université de Bretagne Sud - France, Université Libre de Bruxelles - Belgium, University of Tartu - Estonia).
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: Leading European centers in cybersecurity, cryptology, and digital defense; direct ties to NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE).
available_majors: Track 1: IoT Cybersecurity (UBS France & ULB Belgium)
Track 2: Software & System Cybersecurity (UBS France & University of Tartu Estonia)
Common Semester 1 (UBS): Foundations of Cybersecurity & Network Defense
Semester 4: Master Thesis Internship with Industrial Partner or Research Lab
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Bachelor degree in Computing/Engineering (CGPA >= 3.30/4.00), official IELTS (min 6.5) or TOEFL (min 90), CV, statement of purpose, two academic references via online portal.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: Single consolidated application for the entire consortium; strong competition on networking and security concepts.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Highlight hands-on security experience (CTF challenges, reverse engineering, cryptographic implementations, network defense tools) in your statement.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the CYBERUS portal, select mobility track preference (IoT Cybersecurity or Software Cybersecurity), upload transcripts, CV, statement of purpose, English test score, and register two referees before January 15.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Review CYBERUS tracks, curriculum modules, and admission criteria on master-cyberus.eu.
Step 2: Prepare attested academic transcripts, degree certificate, Europass CV, statement of purpose, and IELTS/TOEFL scorecard.
Step 3: Register on the CYBERUS online application portal.
Step 4: Complete application form and submit all documents before January 15.
Step 5: Consortium Selection Committee reviews applications and scores candidates based on academic and technical backgrounds.
Step 6: Shortlisted candidates attend an online technical interview in February.
Step 7: Consortium publishes initial ranking and sends scholarship nominations to EACEA in March.
Step 8: Final scholarship award notification delivered in April; visa documentation and acceptance letters dispatched.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated Routing: Single consolidated application for both degree admission and Erasmus Mundus scholarship funding.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by two university academic professors directly via referee invitation link.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Max 2-page statement explaining motivation for cybersecurity, chosen study track, relevant technical projects, and career goals.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Brief outline of desired thesis area within IoT security, network defense, or applied cryptology.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Europass format CV highlighting programming languages, security tools, CTF competitions, and certifications.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical interview with consortium professors probing systems security, networking, and algorithmic knowledge.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 6.5+ (min 6.0 each) or TOEFL iBT 90+ (min 20 each).
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: HEC degree attestation required for Pakistani applicants.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Official English translation for all academic records.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Online submission via CYBERUS consortium portal.

required_documents_checklist.specification: HEC-attested undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related engineering discipline.
Complete transcripts showing all subjects, grades, and CGPA (min 3.30 / 4.00).
Europass format CV highlighting security skills, CTF achievements, tools, and code repositories.
Structured statement of purpose detailing interest in cybersecurity and chosen mobility track.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Emphasize security background and track preference.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Confidential evaluation letters from university professors submitted directly via portal.
Official IELTS (min 6.5) or TOEFL iBT (min 90) certificate.
Clear color copy of valid Pakistani passport.

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Scholarship applications close January 15; self-funded applications accepted until May.

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 45% (Academic performance, mathematical rigor, and computing foundation)
selection_process_and_weights.extracurricular_and_leadership_weight: 5% (Participation in CTFs, cybersecurity hackathons, community engagement)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 25% (Quality of statement of purpose, relevant projects, and research orientation)
selection_process_and_weights.work_experience_weight: 5% (Cybersecurity internships, network administration, or software engineering)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 10% (Clarity of vision and alignment with consortium tracks)
selection_process_and_weights.interview_weight: 5% (Online technical interview probing networking and systems security)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: Joint Academic Selection Committee comprising professors from UBS, ULB, and UT.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Consortium scoring grid evaluating previous curriculum match, GPA, SOP, references, and interview performance.

competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~5% to 8% among qualified computer science and cybersecurity graduates
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Graduates in computer science or cybersecurity with solid knowledge of networks, Linux kernel, C programming, and cryptography.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates from FAST-NUCES, NUST, Air University (Cybersecurity Center), and GIKI.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, India, Nigeria, Brazil, Turkey, Colombia, Vietnam, Indonesia.

fake_websites_and_scams: Only apply via the official CYBERUS portal https://master-cyberus.eu/.
Beware of fraudulent consultants claiming backdoor entry into Erasmus Mundus programs.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Applying for the CYBERUS Erasmus Mundus scholarship is completely free.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: No recruitment agencies or educational consultants are affiliated with the CYBERUS consortium.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Apostille and HEC degree attestation charges in Pakistan: ~PKR 15,000 - 25,000.
Initial visa application fee in Islamabad prior to arrival (reimbursed via €1,000 installation grant).
Transit travel between consortium partner countries (subsidized by €3,000/year travel grant).
misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: You must hold an OSCP certification to apply. Reality: Strong academic foundation in computer networks, operating systems, and discrete mathematics is what is evaluated.
Myth: Instruction is in French or Estonian. Reality: All coursework across UBS, ULB, and UT is delivered 100% in English.
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial sources claim MOI is acceptable; the CYBERUS consortium strictly enforces official IELTS or TOEFL score reports.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must successfully earn 60 ECTS credits each academic year to progress between mobility tracks.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Mandatory full-time attendance across all consortium university modules and partner cybersecurity workshops.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Joint Consortium Academic Board monitoring at the end of each semester.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Scholars may not engage in full-time outside employment that compromises academic participation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None; zero service bond or return obligation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Revocation of scholarship and recovery of unspent funds in case of withdrawal or academic misconduct.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_university: Mobility tracks are determined upon admission; changes permitted only under exceptional academic circumstances with board approval.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Not applicable to joint master's programme.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Funding is strictly capped at 24 months.
